desc: Taiwan's largest online retailer, selling consumer goods and electronics through the momo shopping site, app and TV shopping channel.
markets: Almost entirely Taiwan, with a large home delivery network and mobile app; no verified expansion plans
rationale: Taiwan-only retailer with little need for global exposure; an F1 tie could lift shopper awareness in Asia but fit is weak.

desc: Indonesian packaged food maker behind Kopiko coffee candy, Torabika instant coffee, Energen cereal drinks and Danisa biscuits, exported widely.
markets: Indonesia core market; exports to over 90 countries across Asia, Africa, Middle East and Europe; Kopiko is strong in Southeast Asia and the Philippines
rationale: Kopiko and Torabika could build recognition in Southeast Asia and the Middle East through F1 races in Singapore and Abu Dhabi.

desc: Operator and franchisor of CU, South Korea's largest convenience store chain, with thousands of stores plus overseas licensed networks.
markets: South Korea core; CU stores in Mongolia, Malaysia and Kazakhstan under master franchise deals, with further Asian expansion pursued
rationale: Retail brand with growing Asian footprint; F1 offers brand awareness in Korea and Southeast Asia, though a domestic retailer with modest sponsorship needs.

desc: Thai consumer goods maker best known for M-150 energy drink, also selling Shark and Lipovitan drinks and personal care.
markets: Thailand core; M-150 sold in Cambodia, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos and Philippines, with expansion across Southeast Asia
rationale: Energy drink brand with motorsport-friendly image; Thai Grand Prix interest and Southeast Asia awareness, though Red Bull and Monster already occupy the category.

desc: Hong Kong manufacturer of electronic learning toys for children and cordless telephones, plus contract electronics manufacturing for other brands.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with North America the largest market; no verified expansion plans
rationale: Family-oriented toy brand with large US and European retail reach; F1's growing family audience and Mattel and Lego precedents give a plausible fit.

desc: Korean fashion company that owns and operates MLB and Discovery Expedition apparel brands, with large retail presence in China.
markets: South Korea and China main markets, with MLB expanding in Southeast Asia, Hong Kong and Japan and shop openings across Asia
rationale: Youth streetwear brand growing across Asia; F1 offers lifestyle exposure to young fans in China and Southeast Asia through apparel tie-ins.

desc: Thai energy drink maker behind Carabao Dang, which sponsors English football's League Cup and has distribution across Asia and Europe.
markets: Thailand core; exports to Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, China, Vietnam and Europe, with UK sports sponsorships used for brand building
rationale: Energy drink with a track record of global sports sponsorship; F1 would extend UK football visibility into Asia and Europe.

desc: Korean food maker known for Shin Ramyun instant noodles and snacks, with manufacturing plants in the US and China.
markets: South Korea core; plants in the US and China, exports to over 100 countries, with a second US factory and Europe push
rationale: Shin Ramyun is expanding in the US and Europe; F1 offers family-audience exposure in new markets and hospitality for retail partners.

desc: Thai seafood producer owning canned tuna brands including Chicken of the Sea, John West and Petit Navire.
markets: Sells in the US, Europe, Middle East and Asia through owned brands and private label; growing pet food and ingredient business
rationale: Brand portfolio in US and European grocery could use F1 for consumer reach, though a commodity food business with limited marketing appetite.

desc: Korean company owning the Fila sportswear and footwear brand and Fila Korea, plus a stake in golf group Acushnet.
markets: Fila sells in South Korea, China, the US, Europe and across Asia, with growth in golf and tennis apparel and licensed stores
rationale: Heritage sportswear brand seeking relevance with younger consumers in Asia and US; F1 team apparel partnership could broaden lifestyle reach.

desc: Chinese platform for trading, repairing and recycling used consumer electronics, operating the Aihuishou marketplace and AHS Device stores.
markets: China, with growing overseas business reselling used devices through its Paipai platform in Hong Kong, Europe and Japan
rationale: Recommerce brand with sustainability positioning; F1 could build consumer awareness, but its business is China-focused with modest global ambition.

desc: Korean packaged food maker known for Jin Ramen, Ottogi Curry, mayonnaise and sauces, selling in Korea and overseas markets.
markets: South Korea core; exports to the US, China, Vietnam, Australia and Europe, with Ottogi America and overseas production in Vietnam
rationale: Ramen and sauces brand growing abroad; F1 could add global exposure for Korean food, though marketing culture is conservative.

desc: Hong Kong maker of Vitasoy soy milk and Vita tea drinks, sold in Hong Kong, China, Australia and North America.
markets: Hong Kong and mainland China core; Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and North America, with expansion in Southeast Asia and Vita Tea sales
rationale: Plant-based drink brand targeting health-conscious consumers in Asia and the West; F1 races in Singapore and Australia offer regional visibility.

desc: Singapore-headquartered operator of Haidilao hot pot restaurants outside mainland China, with outlets across Asia, North America, Europe and Australia.
markets: Restaurants in Singapore, Southeast Asia, Japan, Korea, North America, Europe and Australia, with continued new store openings planned
rationale: Hot pot chain pushing into Western cities; F1 hospitality and fan visibility around Singapore, Las Vegas and Miami could support brand awareness.

desc: Indonesian e-commerce company operating the Bukalapak marketplace, focused on digital goods and micro-merchants through its Mitra partner network.
markets: Indonesia only, with a pivot toward virtual products and small shop partners; no verified expansion plans
rationale: Indonesian-focused marketplace with little overseas business; F1 offers awareness but little commercial payoff, so fit is weak.

desc: Taiwanese bicycle maker producing Merida bikes and e-bikes, and a long-time minority shareholder of US bike brand Specialized.
markets: Sells Merida bikes in Europe, Asia and the Americas, with factories in Taiwan, China and Europe and growing e-bike business
rationale: Premium bicycle brand with global distribution; ties to Specialized already in F1 and a cycling-enthusiast audience provide technology and brand fit.
f1: Specialized (Merida holds a minority stake) - Formula 1 partner

desc: Chinese online game developer behind Eudemons Online, also running Promethean education technology and the Edmodo learning platform.
markets: China core with games and education products sold in the US, UK and other markets through Promethean and its education arm
rationale: Gaming and education technology brand with limited consumer profile; F1 could showcase games to young fans but relevance is modest.

desc: Korean game publisher best known for Ragnarok Online and its mobile successors, licensed across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
markets: South Korea, Southeast Asia, Japan, Taiwan, North America and Europe via local publishing partners, with new mobile Ragnarok titles
rationale: Game franchise with loyal Asian audience; F1 offers launch exposure for new Ragnarok titles, though budget is small and marketing largely digital.
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of GungHo Online Entertainment

desc: Hong Kong casual clothing retailer selling Giordano basics through hundreds of stores across Asia and the Middle East, mostly franchised.
markets: Hong Kong, mainland China, Taiwan, Southeast Asia and the Middle East through directly operated and franchised shops
rationale: Value apparel brand with Asian and Middle East stores; F1 team apparel could reach fans, but its scale and positioning are modest.

desc: Chinese e-commerce service provider that runs online stores, logistics and digital marketing in China for international and domestic consumer brands.
markets: Mainland China, serving foreign brands entering Tmall and JD, plus its own brand management business; no verified expansion plans
rationale: B2B services firm serving brands in China; F1 hospitality could help meet global brand clients, but consumer fit is weak.

desc: Chinese beauty group behind Perfect Diary color cosmetics, Little Ondine and Galenic skincare, sold mainly through online platforms.
markets: China core, with Perfect Diary sold in Southeast Asia, the UK and elsewhere, plus acquired French skincare brand Galenic
rationale: Young-consumer cosmetics brand seeking overseas growth; F1's growing female audience and global events could support brand awareness in Europe and Asia.

desc: Chinese maker of electric scooters and mopeds sold in China and exported to Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia.
markets: China core, with sales in Europe, Southeast Asia and Latin America through distributors and online stores; new overseas models planned
rationale: Urban electric mobility brand with technology image; F1 could build awareness among young riders in Europe and Asia.

desc: Singapore-headquartered cross-border online retailer selling apparel, home goods and other products to consumers worldwide through LightInTheBox and Miniinthebox sites.
markets: Online customers in Europe, North America and other regions, supplied from Chinese manufacturers; no verified expansion plans
rationale: Small online retailer with global consumers but a low-cost model and limited budget; F1 partnership unlikely to pay off.
